description: An AWS Lambda MicroVM, run from a MicroVM image with the Lambda MicroVMs RunMicrovm call. AWS has no call that changes a MicroVM, so every property is create-only. AWS terminates a MicroVM at its maximum duration, or after it stays suspended for its idle policy's suspended duration, and the next deploy then runs a new one.

IdlePolicy.description: When the MicroVM suspends, resumes, and terminates for lack of traffic.

AutoResumeEnabled.description: Whether a suspended MicroVM resumes when it receives a request.

MaxIdleDurationSeconds.description: How long, in seconds, the MicroVM can be idle before AWS suspends it.

SuspendedDurationSeconds.description: How long, in seconds, the MicroVM can stay suspended before AWS terminates it.

CloudWatchLogging.description: Where in CloudWatch Logs the MicroVM sends its logs.

Logging.description: The MicroVM's logging: CloudWatch, or Disabled to turn logging off. Set exactly one.

MicrovmId.description: The ID of the MicroVM, which AWS assigns.

ImageIdentifier.description: The name or ARN of the MicroVM image to run. AWS reports it as the image's ARN.

ImageVersion.description: The version of the image to run. AWS picks one when the template leaves it out.

ExecutionRoleArn.description: The ARN of the IAM role the MicroVM assumes while it runs.

IngressNetworkConnectors.description: The ARNs of the network connectors that let traffic reach the MicroVM.

EgressNetworkConnectors.description: The ARNs of the network connectors the MicroVM can reach out through.

MaximumDurationInSeconds.description: How long, in seconds, the MicroVM can exist before AWS terminates it.

RunHookPayload.description: Data for this MicroVM that AWS sends as the body of the image's /run hook, such as a session ID or a secret reference.

ImageArn.description: The ARN of the image the MicroVM runs.

Endpoint.description: The HTTPS endpoint of the MicroVM.

StateReason.description: Why the MicroVM is in its state.
